title: How long a governor's term is, and when it starts, in the forty-nine states the game has not read
usableAnswer: A row per state: term length in years, the constitutional or statutory citation establishing it, the commencement rule in the form the game already uses (which weekday, which ordinal week, which month, any offset in days), the election cycle length and one reference year in which a regular gubernatorial election was held. whyItMatters: Measured today at main `1c4992e8`: `stateExecutiveTermRule` in `src/simulation/nationwide-world/state-executive-term-rules.ts` holds a `VERIFIED` map with exactly one entry, Washington. Every other state falls through to `STATE_EXECUTIVE_GAME_PROFILE`, which is a flat `termYears: 4` with a January commencement and a four-year cycle referenced to 2026. Run against the real function: NH 4 (basis game-profile, 0 sources), VT 4 (game-profile, 0 sources), KY 4, TX 4, WA 4 (verified, 3 sources). **New Hampshire and Vermont governors serve two-year terms.** So the game is currently wrong about two states as a matter of law, not as a matter of balance, and it is unverified about forty-nine. answer.summary:
A 52-row table (50 states, the D.C. mayor, the Puerto Rico governor) giving term, reference year and cycle, general-election day, term start, official source and evidence status. Odd-year elections: Kentucky, Louisiana and Mississippi (reference 2027) and New Jersey and Virginia (2025). Two-year terms: New Hampshire and Vermont. Louisiana holds its primary on the third-to-last Saturday in October with a general six Saturdays later if needed; its 2026 Act 414 concerns term limits, not the calendar (corrected against La. Rev. Stat. 18:402). Reference 2024: DE, IN, MO, MT, ND, UT, WA, WV, PR; reference 2028: NC. Alaska and Hawaii terms start the first Monday in December at noon. Direct official text for the start date was found for DE, FL, AK, HI, LA, ME, VA and WA; most other start dates are marked 'UNVERIFIED candidate'. Only Washington is a verified runtime row in state-executive-term-rules.ts.

## A10 — NH/VT are ready to stop using a four-year fallback

**Question:** `governor-term-length-outside-washington` — partial factual delivery.

New Hampshire RSA653:1.I establishes a two-year governor term. Vermont Constitution chapterII§49 establishes two years with a chosen-and-qualified commencement and the specified successor/adjournment conditions. Its legislative January weekday in§46 is not a governor commencement rule.

The two rows are actionable duration evidence but not full qualification/calendar packs. NH's exact commencement and the other states' complete instrument/cycle rows remain to compile. Illinois official retrieval failed and an indexed proposed amendment is not a valid replacement for current constitutional text. Do not claim all49states complete, or change a source's event-bound condition into a fabricated weekday because the current type only supports weekdays.
